content:
Hi everyone,

I've been thinking about having notation for Ideal.span with one or few elements. To me, if we want notation, there are two obvious choices:

  • R ∙ x would mimic the notation coming from Modules. I would propose to have these two notations scoped with the ideal version having higher priority. (At the moment the module notation is not scoped.)
  • ⟪x₁,x₂,...,xₙ⟫ this would have the advantage of allowing multiple generators, but has these funny brackets.

What do you think? Is this something we want? It would definitely make my code and infoview more readable.

Feel free to suggest something if you have a better idea!

/poll Notation for Ideal.span
R ∙ x
⟪x₁,x₂,...,xₙ⟫
No notation - keep things as they are.
See #mathlib4 > global notation for linear span of singleton @ 💬

See #36217 for an example of what the ⟪x₁,x₂,...,xₙ⟫ notation would look like.
I have marked it marked it awaiting-zulip for now .

I've given the PR a review, and the code looks good. I'd be happy to have this notation.

Maybe it would be worth thinking about other similar cases where such a notation could make sense, such as docs#vectorSpan and docs#affineSpan. If we want to use a similar notation there, are we happy to simply scope each notation in a separate namespace? Or is there a better solution that allows these notations to co-exist? This also clashes with the notation for real and complex inner products, which are both also namespaced.

Another point is how to do a type annotation. The PR currently has ⟪1 : α⟫, but we could also go for ⟪1⟫_α, which is analogous to the general inner product notation.
I don't like this notation because nothing in the notation indicates an Ideal
Isn't it similar to the notation {1,2,3} which doesn't tell you what kind of container you are constructing?
no, because those are polymorphic across containers
Well that's exactly what I was suggesting in my message, that the notation could be made polymorphic.
Can I say I don't like polymorphic annotations because it forces me to add long type annotation when lean is confused?

Regarding (R ∙ x : Ideal R), I think you can already use it as an Ideal R.

Although, I'm not saying you want to... might get unwanted side effects using this type of defeq... would be interested to learn if you run into problems using it.

import Mathlib

variable [Ring R] (x : R)

example : Ideal.span { x } = R ∙ x := rfl   -- equality in `(Ideal R)`

example : R ∙ x = Ideal.span { x } := rfl -- equality in `(Submodule R R) `

(regarding "scoping the notation", imo that's often a good idea, regardless of the rest of the discussion)
I tried this for a bit and it would break my simp calls because it would convert my ideals to submodules. This is one of the reasons I proposed this change.
However I dont remember if I had a type ascription, maybe that would work.
Wait, why is Ideal.span not an abbrev for Sumodule.span?
I thought it is exactly that
docs#Ideal.span
why is it a def

I want to unify all of these closure operations soon TM
Does anyone have any thoughts on the notation?
As in, you want to make a single definition with some type class assumption, which subsumes all of Ideal.span, Submodule.span, vectorSpan and affineSpan?

I want to unify the definitions of all the "substructure closure operators"
or more precisely, maps from types of sets to types of substructures which are adjoint (in the sense of posets / Galois connections) to the forgetful map (the coercion to sets)
#mathlib4 > Abstracting the substructure lattice construction
In that case, it may make more sence to wait until that has been done, and then we can introduce a new polymorphic notation based on that.
My capacity to contribute to Mathlib is highly variable. I would recommend not waiting for me. But I did want to say that I am working on unifying stuff.
Well, the implementation of such a polymorphic notation isn't really possible unless the underlying constant is also polymorphic :upside_down:
you could make the notation elaborate to different constants depending on the expected type
@Artie Khovanov are you sure that such a refactor won't cause issues with inferring the type of the polymorphic constant, which I think is what @Weiyi Wang is worried about?
Yes, this is absolutely a concern - I guess we should continue the discussion in the other topic
Based on the vote and discussion, I have closed #36217. Thanks for voting!

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

In that case, it may make more sence to wait until that has been done, and then we can introduce a new polymorphic notation based on that.

I no longer think this notation should be polymorphic. And my new plan is to put the abstracted material behind a new typeclass like ConcreteClosureOperator, so nothing will have to change downstream unless we want it to.

We already have such notation for the intermediate field closure operator R⟮x, y, z⟯, and are about to have notation for the subalgebra closure operator R[x, y, z], so there's definitely precedent here.

The annoying thing in the submodule case is specifying the base ring in a nice place. The best idea I have is ⟪x, y, z⟫_R. Does that parse properly? Maybe we should use different brackets to avoid clashing with inner product notation?

And yeah surely the ideal span should just be an abbrev. I wonder what goes wrong if you make the change.
Testing out making Ideal.span an abbrev: #38145
